title: Static and Terminal
premise: Ivo Ravensworth is a clone of the murdered colony founder, sent to Terminal Station to close a case no one wants solved and to quietly certify the dying settlement for decommission. As she investigates her original's death, she uncovers that the founder faked evidence of an alien signal to keep two rival fleets from warring over the system—and the children's shared dream is the signal still transmitting through them. When the fleets arrive to claim or destroy the truth, Ivo must choose between exposing the lie (and igniting war) or becoming its new keeper. She ends the case by ruling the founder's death an accident, inheriting not just his name but his burden: she stays on Terminal as the lie's living archive, finally visible, finally home.
about_author: Ivo Hartwell is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dead frequencies in remote listening posts before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about people who inherit other people's unfinished business.

chapters.title: Arrival Manifest
chapters.summary: Ivo arrives at Terminal Station under official seal, carrying her predecessor's case files and his face. POV: Ivo. The station master greets her with open grief and closed doors. Emotional beat: alienation—she is a stranger wearing a dead man's welcome.

chapters.title: The Case That Outlived Him
chapters.summary: Reviewing the murder file in her quarters, Ivo finds gaps: no weapon, no motive, witnesses who contradict themselves politely. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into unease as she realizes everyone here has rehearsed their answers.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet Deck
chapters.summary: Ivo tours the colony school and notices the children watching her without fear, as if they expected her. A girl named Sef says, 'You came back wrong.' POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath bureaucratic routine.

chapters.title: Forty-One Years of Static
chapters.summary: Station engineer Oduya shows Ivo the comms array—dead for decades except for a low carrier wave nobody can source or shut off. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: wonder curdling; the static sounds almost like breathing.

chapters.title: His Handwriting, Her Hand
chapters.summary: Comparing the founder's final notes to her own writing, Ivo finds a half-erased page about 'the Dream' and a warning: 'If they ask what the children see, say nothing.' POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the case becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Isn't
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews Mara Voss, the founder's partner, who treats Ivo with tenderness that feels like accusation. Mara says the founder died happy. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: grief displaced onto a copy; loyalty beginning to look like a cage.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: A fleet courier delivers orders: certify Terminal for evacuation within six months. The station council begs Ivo to delay. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: she holds strangers' survival in a signature.

chapters.title: Sef's Dream, First Telling
chapters.summary: Sef describes the shared dream: a lattice of light under the ice, a voice counting down in no human language. Twelve children report identical details. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: innocence carrying an unbearable inheritance.

chapters.title: The Fleet Question
chapters.summary: Ivo learns why the founder's lie matters: two rival fleets both believe the system holds first-contact proof, and the founder's forged evidence is all that keeps them from a standoff. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the scale of the secret lands.

chapters.title: Autopsy of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the founder's last day from logs, Ivo finds he visited the array alone at night, twice, the week he died. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: obsession taking root—she is investigating herself.

chapters.title: Oduya's Confession
chapters.summary: Engineer Oduya admits he helped fake the signal evidence years ago and has kept the array humming ever since. He doesn't know if anything real is underneath. POV: Oduya. Emotional beat: guilt as maintenance work.

chapters.title: Council of the Kept Lie
chapters.summary: The station council reveals they've known for a generation: the lie is the colony's load-bearing wall. They ask Ivo to certify the station healthy and leave. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: complicity offered as kindness.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo descends to the subglacial survey vault and finds the founder's private instruments—pointed inward, recording the colonists themselves. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: betrayal and awe entangled.

chapters.title: Mara Breaks
chapters.summary: Mara confesses the founder was dying of radiation sickness and staged his own death to make the mystery unignorable—a martyrdom to protect the lie. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: love revealed as an elaborate alibi.

chapters.title: The Second Courier
chapters.summary: Both rival fleets announce inspection visits, weeks apart. If their findings disagree, doctrine mandates escalation. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: countdown pressure begins.

chapters.title: Dream Census
chapters.summary: Ivo secretly interviews every child; the dream is evolving—now it includes a figure with her face standing in the lattice. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: the signal knows her; invisibility is over.

chapters.title: Carrier Wave Decoded
chapters.summary: Working nights with Oduya, Ivo isolates structure in the static: prime sequences, then something like grammar. It predates the founder's forgery by centuries. POV: Oduya. Emotional beat: the lie may have been built on a truth.

chapters.title: The Original's Letters
chapters.summary: In the vault, Ivo finds letters the founder wrote to his clone—the one being written now. He apologizes for the face, the case, the choice he's handing down. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: inheritance as ambush and gift at once.

chapters.title: First Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: The Concordat inspectors land, courteous and thorough. Their lead examiner, Halvorsen, requests all child dream reports. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: polite menace; the room gets smaller.

chapters.title: Buying Six Days
chapters.summary: Ivo stalls with doctored medical records while the children's dreams accelerate—they now dream in sync with the array's pulses. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: she lies fluently for the first time and hates how good it feels.

chapters.title: Sef Runs
chapters.summary: Sef, terrified of being taken for study, flees to the ice with three others. Search parties fan out in a whiteout. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: fear of adults who were supposed to be safe.

chapters.title: Found in the Lattice
chapters.summary: Ivo finds the children at the survey vault entrance, unharmed, pointing to frost patterns matching the dream exactly. Something under the ice is answering. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: awe overriding protocol.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Offer
chapters.summary: Halvorsen privately tells Ivo he knows the evidence is forged—and offers to bury her fraud if she delivers the children to Concordat custody. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Council Splits
chapters.summary: Half the council wants to confess everything and evacuate; the rest would rather die keeping the secret. Oduya stands in the middle, holding the array keys. POV: Oduya. Emotional beat: found family fracturing under weight.

chapters.title: Second Fleet on Approach
chapters.summary: The Meridian fleet arrives early and unannounced, weapons cold but visible. Both examiners now sit in the same room, comparing notes. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the standoff the founder feared, materialized.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Copy
chapters.summary: Under joint questioning, Ivo walks a razor: admitting forgery exists while refusing to say who made it or why. Halvorsen nearly breaks her; the Meridian examiner, Vane, watches too carefully. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: identity as shield and target.

chapters.title: Vane's Truth
chapters.summary: Vane reveals Meridian has known about the real signal for years and let the lie stand because peace was cheaper than proof. He proposes joint silence. POV: Vane. Emotional beat: cynicism that is almost wisdom.

chapters.title: The Children Testify
chapters.summary: Refusing custody, the children speak as one before both fleets, reciting the dream's newest verse: coordinates, and a date. The date is nine days out. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: the smallest voices forcing the largest choices.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Ivo commits: instead of hiding the signal, she'll verify it publicly—if it's real, both fleets must stand down together; if not, she takes the fall alone. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: resolve replacing fear.

chapters.title: Excavation
chapters.summary: Colonists and rival crews dig side by side toward the lattice's source. Old grudges surface and are set aside; Oduya's array becomes the expedition's heart. POV: Oduya. Emotional beat: enemies becoming crew.

chapters.title: What the Founder Knew
chapters.summary: Deep in the vault, Ivo deciphers the founder's final letter fully: he had confirmed the signal was real and real means answerable—he died ensuring someone would finish the conversation. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: forgiveness of the dead.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: A Concordat hardliner sabotages the excavation; a collapse traps Sef and two workers. Halvorsen's cover begins to crack. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: terror underground, trust tested in the dark.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Lattice
chapters.summary: Ivo leads the rescue through the dream's geography—which turns out to be a map. They reach Sef as the lattice lights around them, responding to presence. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the dream made solid; found family forged in ice.

chapters.title: The Answering Machine
chapters.summary: They reach the source: an ancient receiver, still listening, built by hands unknown. It isn't broadcasting—it's waiting for a reply. The countdown ends tomorrow. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: humility before vast patience.

chapters.title: Fleets at Defcon
chapters.summary: With hours left, both fleets go to alert, each convinced the other will seize the site. Ivo broadcasts the whole truth—forgery, signal, and all—to both fleets simultaneously. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: the lie dies so the truth might live.

chapters.title: Climax: One Voice
chapters.summary: At the receiver, Ivo sends the reply using the children's dream-language, with both fleets watching the same feed. The lattice answers with a star map—not conquest, an invitation to witness. Standdown orders ripple outward. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into communion.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Confession
chapters.summary: Ivo faces inquiry for the founder's fraud and her own concealments. Halvorsen testifies unexpectedly in her favor; Vane argues the peace held, whatever the paperwork says. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: judgment tempered by grace.

chapters.title: Ruling: Accident
chapters.summary: Ivo closes the forty-year case, ruling the founder's death an accident of his own design—an act of love misfiled as murder. Mara finally mourns properly. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief released after decades.

chapters.title: Certification
chapters.summary: Ivo certifies Terminal Station—but as viable, not doomed. Fleets negotiate joint stewardship; colonists choose to stay. The children's dream fades to ordinary sleep. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: a future chosen rather than inherited.

chapters.title: Static and Terminal
chapters.summary: One year later, Ivo remains as the station's recorder, logging the ongoing dialogue with the listeners below. She signs her log not as the founder's copy but as herself. POV: Ivo. Emotional beat: belonging earned—visible at last, and home.
